title: Where Snappr Fits In
summary: Snappr sells business photography services three ways: pay-as-you-go, Pro, and Enterprise. Here's how to pick the right tier for your shoot volume.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways


- Snappr sells photography three ways: **pay-as-you-go, Pro, and Enterprise** . Volume decides which one fits, not budget.
- **Pay-as-you-go** is free with a 15% service fee. Right for occasional shoots, and worth staying on if that is you.
- **Pro** cuts the fee to 9% and adds a three-seat workspace, saved creative guidelines, and smart image search. United States only.
- **Enterprise** removes the service fee and adds API access, central editing, and dedicated account management for monthly volume.
- The signal to move up is coordination, not spend: repeated briefs, multiple bookers, and images that feed a system.


Most companies buy photography the same way at four shoots a year as they do at 40. That is the mistake, and it is an expensive one.


‍


Business photography services come in three shapes at Snappr: pay-as-you-go, Pro, and Enterprise. They are not good, better, and best. Each answers a different question about how often you shoot and how many people touch the result.


## Why Buying Photography Breaks As You Grow


At low volume, the hard part is finding someone: a competent photographer, in the right city, on the right day, at a price you can predict. Solve that and you are done.


‍


At higher volume, finding someone stops being the problem and new ones take its place. You brief every photographer from scratch. Output drifts between locations because nobody wrote down what on-brand looks like, and generic images[get skipped the way banner ads do](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/photos-as-web-content/) . Two people book the same shoot twice. None of that is a booking problem, and booking faster will not fix it. That is where the way you buy has to change.


## The Three Ways Businesses Buy Photography


Snappr's three tiers map to three stages of that shift. Volume is the axis that matters, so read them in order and stop at the one that sounds like your calendar.


### Pay-As-You-Go: When Photography Is Occasional


Pay-as-you-go is free to join, with a 15% service fee per shoot. It is built for individuals and businesses with low-volume needs: a headshot refresh, a new menu, one property, a single event. You[book a shoot](https://www.snappr.com/shoots) , you pay for that shoot, and nothing carries over.


‍


One login, no contract, no annual fee. If you handle photography a few times a year, this is the correct answer, and upgrading would cost you money for features you would never open.


‍


Most Snappr customers start here, and plenty of them should stay.


*Exactly the job pay-as-you-go was built for: book it, pay for it, done.*


### Snappr Pro: When Photography Becomes A Habit


> Pay-as-you-go works when photography is occasional. When it's weekly, you need more than bookings.


‍


[Snappr Pro](https://www.snappr.com/pro) is an annual membership, currently $49 for the first year against a regular price of $99. It cuts the service fee on every booking from 15% to 9%, which is where most of the value sits. Members save more than 5% on every shoot, so the membership pays for itself within a handful of bookings.


‍


The rest of Pro turns repeat shoots into a system:


- A three-seat workspace, so booking is not trapped in one person's account
- Saved creative guidelines, so you brief once instead of every time
- Favorite and blocked photographers, so whoever nailed it last time comes back
- Smart image search across your gallery, plus bulk AI image generation


‍


It suits multi-location brands, marketing teams, and[eCommerce brands](https://www.snappr.com/use-cases/ecommerce-and-fashion) shooting[new product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350) regularly. Pro is available in the United States only. For the full feature list and how it was built, read[the Snappr Pro launch post](https://www.snappr.com/blog/snappr-pro) .


*Dental groups, franchises, and retail chains hit Pro first: same brief, different address, over and over.*


### Enterprise: When Photography Becomes Infrastructure


[Snappr Enterprise](https://www.snappr.com/enterprise) is for companies needing multiple photoshoots or many pieces of visual content per month, where photography has stopped being a task and started being a supply line.


‍


There is no service fee. Pricing is a custom annual contract with credits scaled to your volume, which makes high-frequency shooting predictable to budget. What you get is control at the organization level:


- API access and no-code workflow automation, so shoots trigger from your own systems
- Shoots centrally edited, so every location returns one look
- End-customer scheduling and communications, so Snappr handles the back and forth with tenants, sellers, or venues
- Expert-assisted creative guidelines, unlimited seats with advanced permissions, custom reports, and dedicated account management


‍


This is the tier behind Bring a Trailer's 30,000+ photoshoots and Redfin's shoots across 150+ cities. 73% of the Fortune 500 have used Snappr.


*At Enterprise volume a product shot is not a project. It is a row in a catalog that refreshes on a schedule.*


## How To Choose Business Photography Services By Volume


Three questions settle it faster than a pricing page will.


‍


**Is anyone repeating a brief?** If you have explained your brand's look to more than two photographers, saved creative guidelines will pay you back before the fee discount does.


‍


**Is more than one person booking?** A single login is fine for one marketer. It breaks the moment a colleague needs to see what was shot, or a regional manager books without telling anyone.


‍


**Does photography feed a system?** If images populate[listings](https://support.google.com/business/answer/6103862) ,[menus](https://www.snappr.com/use-cases/menus-and-restaurants) , or a product catalog, you want shoots triggered by your software rather than by a person remembering. That is an Enterprise question, and it arrives sooner than most teams expect.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What Is The Difference Between Pay-As-You-Go And Snappr Pro?


Pay-as-you-go is free to join and charges a 15% service fee per shoot, with one login and no saved settings. Pro is an annual membership that drops the fee to 9% and adds a three-seat workspace, saved creative guidelines, favorite and blocked photographers, smart image search, and bulk AI generation. The fee difference alone is why most teams move.


### How Much Do Business Photography Services Cost Through Snappr?


Prices depend on the shoot type, the location, and the session length, and you can see live prices in the booking flow before you commit. Your tier changes what sits on top: 15% on pay-as-you-go, 9% on Pro, and no service fee on Enterprise.


### Is Snappr Pro Available Outside The United States?


Not currently. Pro is available in the United States only. Businesses elsewhere can book on pay-as-you-go or talk to Snappr about an Enterprise contract.


### Does Snappr Require An Annual Contract?


Only Enterprise does. Pay-as-you-go carries no commitment at all, and Pro is a flat annual membership with no spend commitment attached to it.


### When Should A Business Move To Enterprise Photography Services?


When photography runs monthly at volume across locations, teams, or listings, and coordinating it has become somebody's actual job. The practical trigger is usually the first time you need shoots to start from your own system rather than a person.
